identity.title: Metabolic engineering of Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) for plasmid-free high-level production of ergothioneine via hybrid pathway and multicopy chromosomal integration.

content.abstract: Ergothioneine (L-ergothioneine, EGT) is an antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective compound with high value in the food, cosmeceutical, and nutraceutical industries. Herein, an efficient microbial cell factory was developed by engineering a hybrid EGT biosynthetic pathway in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) through the synergistic assembly of heterologous genetic modules of prokaryotic and eukaryotic origins. Systematic interrogation of gene combinations and transcriptional architectures identified sulfoxide synthase-mediated oxidative coupling as the pivotal metabolic bottleneck governing EGT biosynthetic flux. Addressing this rate-limiting step allowed the initial plasmid-bearing strain, EGT04, reaching an EGT titer of 156.35 mg/L during shake-flask fermentation. A multicopy chromosomal integration CRISPR-associated transposase strategy was implemented for stable multicopy chromosomal integration. This approach yielded a genetically robust, plasmid-free, and marker-free chassis, EGT15, which achieved an EGT titer of 287.14 mg/L, representing a 127.47% improvement over the initial prototype. Subsequent refinement of the fermentation landscape, integrating optimized glycerol feeding and strategic cysteine supplementation with a two-stage thermal control strategy (biomass accumulation at 37  degrees C followed by induction at 20  degrees C), further elevated the shake-flask titer to 353.69 mg/L. The final scale-up in a 5 L-fed-batch bioreactor culminated in a peak EGT concentration of 8.36 g/L with a volumetric productivity of 0.12 g/L/h. By eliminating the requirements for antibiotics and plasmid maintenance, this high-yielding and stable platform minimizes metabolic drag and enhances the industrial production potential. This study established a robust, plasmid-free, and resistance-free E. coli platform for sustainable microbial manufacturing of EGT, providing a scalable strategy for the high-level production of value-added sulfur-containing compounds.
